chunks: 5028 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Yazid al-Kunasi, who said: I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a woman who married during her waiting period, and he said:

If she married during a waiting period following the death of her husband, before the completion of four months and ten days, then there is no stoning upon her, but she is to receive one hundred lashes. If she married during the waiting period of a divorce in which her husband had the right to take her back, then stoning is upon her. And if she married during a waiting period in which her husband had no right of return over her, then upon her is the punishment of an unmarried adulterer. And if a Christian man fornicates with a Muslim woman, then when he is seized so that the legal punishment may be carried out upon him, he accepts Islam, then the ruling concerning him is that he is to be beaten until he dies, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:

But when they saw Our punishment, they said, 'We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in that which we used to associate with Him.' But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment—such is the sunnah of Allah that has already passed among His servants—and there the falsifiers lost.

key_terms.الرَّجْمَ: stoning as a hadd punishment in the specified legal circumstance
key_terms.الْأَرْبَعَةِ الْأَشْهُرِ وَعَشْرٍ: the waiting period of a widow before remarriage
key_terms.حَدَّ الزَّانِي غَيْرِ الْمُحْصَنِ: the legal punishment of an unmarried adulterer
key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: the husband's right to take back his wife during a revocable divorce
key_terms.سُنَّتَ اللَّهِ: the established way of Allah in dealing with His servants
key_terms.عِدَّةٍ: the legally prescribed waiting period after death or divorce

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying during the 'iddah, and does accepting Islam after arrest remove the hadd punishment?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning a woman who marries during her 'iddah, distinguishing between the waiting period after death, revocable divorce, and irrevocable divorce. It also states a ruling regarding a Christian man who fornicates with a Muslim woman and accepts Islam only after arrest, citing Qur'an 40:84-85 to show that faith professed at the moment of punishment does not avert the legal consequence.
